decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY that adds the Small Block and Big Block tickets to its reward components, while its existing state already identifies the random existing NFT holder as recipient.
The same-message FAQ MODIFY already states that a no-code mint sends the commission and tickets to a random existing NFT holder.
The no-referral recipient rule changes reward allocation behavior, not the amounts or prize-pool destinations governing primary-mint revenue allocation.
Selecting a random existing NFT holder to receive no-referral tickets does not change how prize winners are selected from ticket holders.
The no-referral ticket recipient rule does not change the Big Block prize amount, winner count, pool funding, or draw trigger.
The no-referral ticket recipient rule does not change the Small Block prize amount, winner count, pool funding, or draw condition.
Allocating no-referral tickets to a random existing holder does not change which ticket counters or other attributes must appear in NFT metadata.
The source rule applies when no referral code is used on a primary mint and does not alter secondary-sale royalty enforcement or allocation.
Issuing no-referral rewards to a random existing NFT holder does not change how an NFT's book, referral code, badges, or tickets transfer on resale.
The ticket-recipient rule does not change the manual one-click collection flow for eventual prize winners.
The source preserves the direct-referral commission rule and separately defines fallback allocation when no referral code is used.
The no-referral ticket allocation does not change badge milestones, storage, presentation, or effects.
